title_content.content: When Does a Willingness to Disrupt Itself Pay Off? Downgrade to Equal-weight

paragraph_content.content: CRM is actively disrupting itself to position for the agentic era, but strong Agentforce KPIs have yet to drive an inflection in organic growth as legacy portfolio drags persist. Shares likely to remain range-bound absent a notable growth inflection, leaving R/R balanced at ~19x GAAP P/E. DG to EW.
■ Agentforce KPIs are inflecting, but AI momentum has yet to bend the cRPO/organic rev growth curve as legacy assets (namely Commerce, Tableau) continue to drag
- Believe Salesforce is making the right agentic pivot towards headless, but monetization remains nascent, meaning translation to growth will take time
Margin optionality remains, yet near-term reinvestment in Agentforce, Data 360, and headless likely limits leverage realization, delaying the self-help payoff
At ~19x GAAP P/E, see shares fairly valued absent a notable growth inflection; balanced risk/reward supports EW and reduction in PT to $185
With this note, Adam Wood is assuming lead coverage of Salesforce (CRM) at Equal-weight rating and $185 PT.

Durable Moat & Right Journey, Balanced by Limited Growth Visibility. Recent results have been a 'Tale of Two Cities' for Salesforce, as AI momentum remains offset by continued deterioration and/or lack of upside to Subscription revenue growth and visible forward-looking metrics (Exhibit 3). This disconnect – strong agentic KPIs but lack of inflection in organic growth indicators – has driven material multiple compression in shares and leaves investors zeroed in on one key question: when do Agentforce and new headless monetization initiatives offset the structural drags from underperforming areas of the portfolio (Commerce, Tableau), driving sustained subscription revenue growth? Re-assessing our coverage through our AI-readiness framework, we continue to see Salesforce as having a strong moat and executing on the right path of the 'journey'. Importantly, Salesforce is one of the few scaled SaaS incumbents that appears to be actively trying to disrupt itself – rather than defending only the legacy seat-based UI, management is decoupling the data, workflow, and action layers from its traditional application interface.

paragraph_content.content: Strategically, we view that as likely the correct move, as in an agentic world, Salesforce will increasingly need to make its customer data, context, permissions, and workflow layer the monetizable surface. However, given the nascency of monetization here, we lack the clarity we would need to maintain our prior OW on the prospect of a sustained, improving growth profile at Salesforce near-term, especially as legacy parts of the business should remain drags. Thus, while we believe Salesforce is positioning itself well to transition alongside the agentic world, with more to prove in demonstrating ability to monetize this transition, we see shares remaining largely range-bound absent any notable growth inflection, warranting a move to Equal-weight.

title_content.content: Downgrade to EW on Three Key Points:

paragraph_content.content: 1. AI KPIs Inflecting, But Seeing Minimal P&L Impact as Legacy Areas of Portfolio Drag on Overall Organic Growth. In isolation, data points behind Salesforce's AI portfolio continue to exude momentum, with the company accelerating to 200%+ growth in Agentforce ARR at a now $1B+ scale (Exhibit 1). Moreover, the company is seeing ramping growth in both tokens (+152% QoQ as of 1Q27) and Agentic Work Units (the measure of intelligence / work completed against those tokens, +111% QoQ as of 1Q27), underpinning the momentum in adoption of its solutions. The company has also put forth the argument that power users of AWUs are expanding their spend on Salesforce at a materially faster clip than non AI adopters, beginning to provide support for the monetization scenario presented at Investor Day (Exhibit 2). That being said, conversion of the aforementioned momentum to leading indicators and / or the broader topline has not yet materialized, with Salesforce now posting two consecutive quarters of minimal cRPO upside, a lack of inflection in CC cRPO growth / cRPO-based bookings growth (Exhibit 3), and FY27 organic revenue growth continuing to decelerate towards the high single digits. We believe this is largely a function of varying growth rates within the overall portfolio – specifically, marketing & commerce and integration & analytics clouds have shown weak performance (Exhibit 4). In our view, there are structural weights on these parts of the business, particularly in Commerce, where Shopify has been a rapid market share gainer / disruptor, and Tableau, where lighter-weight business intelligence products likely retain outsized exposure to AI disruption. Given the dynamics of these growth drags, we are hesitant to underwrite a scenario of sustained growth improvement beyond 4Q, where the acquisition of Informatica is being anniversaried (and therefore becomes organic), likely bolstering the company's 2H27 acceleration expectations. Stated differently, while Agentforce is showing encouraging leading indicators, we do not yet have confidence that AI momentum can drive a durable acceleration in organic growth as persistent drags across legacy areas of the portfolio will require sustained strength in newer, better-performing businesses to offset – a mix shift that is likely to take time.

paragraph_content.content: 2. Relative Moat / Journey Strength, Though Transition Still Difficult. In our AI-readiness work, Salesforce scores most constructively in areas such as system-of-record depth, enterprise distribution, proprietary data/context, and domain expertise. Perhaps more importantly, however, we would argue that Salesforce has been relatively front-footed in its willingness to disrupt itself and transition its business model instead of defending the seat-based UI at all costs. Notably, this is a company that has repeatedly been willing to expand, and at times blur, the boundaries of its own franchise – pioneering the SaaS transition, expanding beyond Sales and into adjacent areas of the front office, and now shifting from human-driven UI to agents. This manifests as relatively strong positioning on the 'journey' portion of our score-card relative to other scaled SaaS peers (such as Workday and Adobe). As value shifts from screens and seats toward outcomes and action, Salesforce is trying to move the monetization layer lower in the stack toward the data, metadata, context, permissions and workflow layer agents needed to reason and act across the enterprise.

While we believe the convergence of Informatica, MuleSoft, Data 360, and Slack enable a compelling case for Salesforce assembling the control plane for enterprise agentic AI, we acknowledge strategic correctness is not the same as growth inflection, integral for investors to re-engage with shares here. Thus, the difficulty for Salesforce remains converting agentic activity into predictable subscription growth, and in our view, the pricing path is the clearest signal that this remains too early to underwrite. Salesforce has already changed its AI pricing structure a number of times – moving from conversation-based Agentforce pricing toward more flexible enterprise agreements, action-based constructs and credit-style models as customers push for predictability and value alignment. While our survey work continues to indicate that CIOs see Salesforce constructively as a key partner they plan to leverage in deploying enterprise AI (Exhibit 5), there remains much to prove by means of effective monetization translating to durable growth acceleration, which we think is well evidenced by the longer journey for Salesforce (and SaaS broadly) relative to other areas of Software (Infra, some Security) that are actively seeing topline inflection from AI.

title_content.content: 3. See More Room to Get Efficient Versus Peers; Though Current Investment

paragraph_content.content: Mode Likely Near-Term Overhang. In our efficiency work, Salesforce screens below the cleanest scaled application peers, generating ~$404k of CY25 GAAP gross profit per employee versus ~$839k at Intuit and ~$684k at Adobe (Exhibit 8). There is similar room on the operating profit front, with Salesforce sitting at ~$104k/head versus ~$281k/head at Adobe and ~$280k/head at Intuit (Exhibit 9). We see this supporting the idea that the model can still get more efficient – particularly in GTM productivity, support intensity, and better leverage against a $40B+ revenue base, where Sales & Marketing spend as a % of revenue remains elevated vs peers (Exhibit 10). That said, management commentary continues to point incremental dollars toward growth in the near-term as they look to scale Agentforce, Data 360, and continuing to build out the monetization vehicle behind headless. As such, while there is a self-help angle here, Salesforce is currently choosing to spend through the AI transition rather than fully harvest the model today. Longer-term, however, the company's Rule-of-50 construct by FY30 effectively implies a path toward ~40% non-GAAP operating margins versus the FY27 guide of ~34.3%, suggesting an opportunity for margins to further inflect beyond this investment period.

paragraph_content.content: How Do we See Valuation? CRM currently trades at ~19x GAAP earnings, largely inline with similarly growing peers INTU (~13x), ADBE (~12x), and SAP (~16x) on an absolute basis, though a slight premium to peers on a growth adjusted basis (CRM at ~2.5x vs group at ~1.6x). Thus, the risk/reward feels relatively balanced absent a notable growth inflection.
Exhibit 11: CRM Trades Largely inline With Mature at Scale Peers on a GAAP P/E Basis

Why Not UW? We believe Salesforce's willingness to disrupt itself (lean into headless) demonstrates an understanding of the AI innovation cycle and how traditional, mature Software vendors will need to iterate on their offerings, pricing models, and user interfaces to benefit from AI proliferation. While there are legacy portions of the portfolio that will take time to work through, on a relative basis, we see a more favorable 'Journey' for Salesforce relative to other areas of SaaS. Specifically, Salesforce remains a cleaner strategic asset in our AI-readiness work relative to a name like Adobe, where AI displacement could be more material at lighter-weight creatives, especially as near-term execution risk is heightened. Versus Workday, we could see more downside risk to the multiple given WDAY shares trade richer than CRM shares when factoring in SBC. On the other side of the equation, the biggest risk to our EW (rather than maintaining OW) move would be faster than anticipated monetization / growth in Salesforce's newer strategic initiatives (Agentforce, Headless) more than offsetting underperforming areas, supporting durable growth re-acceleration.

PT to $185. We lower our price target to $185 (from $287 previously) as we now apply a 10X multiple (more ~inline with mature SaaS peers, vs. 15X previously) to our CY28 FCF/share estimate of ~$21. Discounting this back at a 10% WACC results in our $185 price target, which implies ~21x CY27 GAAP P/E.

Double-digit revenue CAGR, benefitting from recent M&A. Stability in Sales & Service Clouds with durable growth in Agentforce and AI initiatives support revenue growing at a ~10% CAGR from FY26-29. Increased competition and legacy portfolio drag on growth. Incremental investments limit margin expansion potential despite increasing opex discipline, limiting margin expansion to ~mid 30s by FY29. Underweight (U). The stock's total return is expected to be below the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.
Unless otherwise specified, the time frame for price targets included in MS is 12 to 18 months.
Attractive (A): The analyst expects the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months to be attractive vs. the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated below.

In-Line (I): The analyst expects the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months to be in line with the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated below. Cautious (C): The analyst views the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months with caution vs. the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated below.
